# Milésimo gol, o último desafio de Messi na reta final da carreira

## Vice-campeão mundial, craque argentino deixa a Copa do Mundo a 81 gols da marca histórica

Por Redação do ge — Nova Iorque, EUA

---

* Aos 39 anos, Lionel Messi busca o milésimo gol na carreira. O craque argentino soma 919 gols oficiais e precisa de mais 81 para atingir a marca histórica.
* No ritmo atual, o argentino pode alcançar o feito até 2028. Em uma contagem estendida com amistosos por clubes, ele já acumula 958 gols na carreira.

## **Quantos gols fez Pelé?**

**Nas principais contagens internacionais, Pelé marcou 767 gols em 831 jogos oficiais** (partidas de competição por clubes e jogos pelo Brasil contra outras seleções principais, de qualquer tipo).

Contando todas as partidas do Rei do Futebol na carreira, o total é de 1.282 gols. Muitos deles, porém, foram marcados contra combinados de clubes ou seleções regionais, além dos realmente discutíveis jogos pela seleção do Exército. Mas se forem considerados os contextos da época, quando o Santos era frequentemente convidado para excursionar pelo mundo em amistosos que lotavam estádios, muitos deles contra alguns dos principais times da Europa e da América do Sul, **é possível fazer um novo recorte, entre a conta internacional e os números enaltecidos no Brasil, confirmando que, sim, Pelé ultrapassou com folga os mil gols na carreira.**

> Contando os amistosos do Santos contra outras equipes profissionais, junto com amistosos do Brasil contra outras seleções principais, além das partidas efetivamente de competição por clubes e seleção brasileira, Pelé teria entre 1.159 e 1.162 gols (não é possível determinar um número exato, porque há fontes conflitantes sobre partidas do início da carreira pelo Santos).

Ainda que se considerem apenas os 767 gols marcados em jogos oficiais, como preferem as estatísticas internacionais, Pelé tem uma média muito superior a de outros jogadores de destaque, como Messi e Cristiano Ronaldo, por exemplo.

## **Primeiro gol oficial em 2005**

Messi marcou seu primeiro gol em jogo oficial pelo Barcelona no dia 1º de maio de 2005, contra o Albacete, pelo Campeonato Espanhol, aos 17 anos e nove meses. Maior ídolo da história do Barça, ele se despediu em 2021 como o recordista de gols na história do clube: 672 em partidas de competição, sem contar amistosos.

Na breve passagem pelo Paris Saint-Germain, Messi marcou 32 gols em duas temporadas. Desde 2023 no Inter Miami, o argentino soma 90 gols em jogos oficiais. Messi é o maior artilheiro da Argentina, com 125 gols em 207 partidas.

## **Com amistosos, Messi tem 958 gols**

Na contagem dos gols de Messi, assim como a de Cristiano Ronaldo, são considerados apenas os gols em jogos de competição por clubes, e todas as partidas pela seleção profissional da Argentina (amistosos e oficiais). Mas Messi também disputou amistosos pelos clubes que defendeu (Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain e Inter Miami), com 39 gols marcados. Portanto, em uma conta "estendida", o argentino já teria 958 gols.

> No caso de Cristiano Ronaldo, por exemplo, se os 46 gols feitos em amistosos de clubes forem considerados, o português já até passou dos mil - ele agora teria 1.022 na carreira.

Messi deixou sua marca em amistosos pelos três clubes em que atuou. No Barcelona, antes do primeiro gol "oficial", ele já tinha feito dois durante a preparação para temporada 2004/05, contra Palamós e Kashima Antlers.

O craque saiu do Barça em 2021, com 32 gols em amistosos válidos (time principal x time principal), sem contar seis marcados contra combinados. No PSG, ele fez dois em amistosos, e já tem cinco pelo Inter Miami, totalizando 39 gols em partidas fora de competição - números que não são considerados pela imprensa internacional na corrida ao milésimo.

Messi também tem 11 gols feitos na base do Barça e 16 em seleções de base e olímpica da Argentina, que também não entram na contagem para o milésimo - com a camisa *albiceleste*, são considerados apenas os jogos de competição e amistosos com a seleção principal.

## Qual foi o gol mais emblemático da carreira de Messi?

Dentre todos os marcados em sua carreira, o gol considerado mais emblemático de Messi é o da Copa do Mundo de 2022, quando a Argentina venceu a França e conquistou o tricampeonato. No entanto, outros gols importantes marcam a carreira de sucesso do argentino.

*   **Gol contra o Getafe em 2007**: Icônico, quando Messi driblou vários jogadores em uma corrida que se assemelha ao famoso gol de Diego Maradona contra a Inglaterra em 1986.
*   **Gol de falta contra o Brasil em 2012**: Destacou sua habilidade em cobranças de falta
*   **Gol contra o Bayern de Munique em 2015**: Um gol que exemplificou sua capacidade de decidir jogos em momentos cruciais, especialmente em competições da Uefa.

## Quem são as maiores vítimas de Messi?

As maiores vítimas de Messi em sua carreira são os times espanhóis: Sevilla, Atlético de Madrid e Valencia. No Sevilla, o argentino marcou 38 gols, já no Atlético de Madrid foram 32 gols. O Valencia completa o pódio, vendo Messi mandar a bola para o fundo das redes em 31 oportunidades.

Os rivais do Barça também não guardaram boas lembranças de Messi. O Real Madrid, principal adversário a nível espanhol e mundial, é o quarto da lista, enquanto o Espanyol, rival local da Catalunha, completa o top-5, com 26 e 25 gols sofridos, respectivamente.

## Quem tem mais gols: Messi ou CR7?

Cristiano Ronaldo tem mais gols que Messi. Enquanto o argentino tem **936 gols marcados**, [CR7 tem**981 gols na carreira**.](https://www.365scores.com/pt-br/news/magazine/quantos-gols-cristiano-ronaldo-tem-na-carreira/)

CR7 é conhecido por ser o **maior artilheiro em atividade no futebol mundial**, com uma carreira que inclui passagens por clubes como Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus, e atualmente Al-Nassr, além de ser o maior artilheiro da seleção portuguesa[](https://ge.globo.com/futebol/futebol-internacional/noticia/2023/10/16/quantos-gols-tem-o-cristiano-ronaldo.ghtml).

Messi, por sua vez, fez a maior parte de seus gols jogando pelo Barcelona, PSG, e atualmente pelo Inter Miami, além de ser o maior artilheiro da seleção argentina.[](https://www.365scores.com/pt-br/news/magazine/gols-de-messi-na-carreira/)

## Messi vs Ronaldo - so who is the best?

**Lionel Messi** and **Cristiano Ronaldo** are two of the best footballers of all time, arguably *the* very best of them all. And remarkably, their careers have largely coincided, with both players dominating the game for well over a decade now. But who is the best?

We compare them both in a number of different categories and let you decide the overall winner.

## Who scores more goals?

What really made this rivalry catch fire was their incredible, unprecedented goalscoring rates, with both Messi and Ronaldo averaging more than one goal every game at their peaks. During the 9 years Ronaldo spent at Real Madrid, **Messi and Ronaldo both scored a goal every 85 minutes** in all competitions. The adjacency of their goalscoring - matching each other blow for blow - has been astounding over the years.

Over their entire careers, it's Messi who edges the ratio, with **0.79 goals per game**, whereas Ronaldo has scored **0.73 goals per game**. If we drill down into goals per minutes, Messi **scores a goal every 104 minutes**, and Ronaldo **scores a goal every 112 minutes**.

Ronaldo still has more **all time career goals** than Messi though (Ronaldo has **981 career goals** and Messi has **936 career goals**), but Ronaldo has played 160 more games over his career than Messi has.

Although Messi shades the overall ratio, Ronaldo spent more of his formative years as a more traditional right winger, only really starting to focus on goalscoring as his primary function in 2006, 3-4 years into his career. For Messi, it was 2-3 years until he completed the transformation from a nippy winger into a player hungry for goals above everything else. If we take these differing beginnings into account, the ratios would be even closer.

Of all the categories, goalscoring is the hardest to separate them on.

## Who provides more assists?

When it comes to assists, there's only one winner. Lionel Messi's playmaking abilities are right up there with the very best, and he has the numbers to prove it.

Messi has racked up an impressive **427 assists in 1181 career appearances**, compared to Ronaldo's **261 assists in 1341 games**.

However, because Messi has a clear ascendancy when it comes to assists, this often leads people to fall into the trap of underestimating Ronaldo's proficiency in this area. Ronaldo's assist numbers are still extremely impressive compared to the other mere mortals that play the beautiful game.

In fact, Ronaldo has more in the **Champions League**, with **41 assists** to Messi's **40 assists** - granted Ronaldo has played 20 more matches than Messi, but this is still an impressive tally.

With that said, you can't ignore Messi's overall assist stats.

## Who's the best at passing?

The passing stats point to a clear winner in this category; Lionel Messi. But again, Ronaldo's passing abilities are often underestimated.

In the games we have this data for, Messi has made **2145 key passes**, whilst Ronaldo has made **1319 key passes**.

Messi also dominates the **throughball** statistics, making **550 successful throughballs**, compared to Ronaldo's **89 successful throughballs**.

Although Messi's passing numbers are clearly superior, Ronaldo's are still impressive. It's also likely that his passing stats would have been significantly higher before 2009 when he was more involved in the creative build-up play.

[More Key Pass Stats](/detailed-stats/key-passes/)

## Who's the best at dribbling?

Ronaldo started his career as a tricky winger, when his game was all about running at and beating defenders with his pace and skill. As he has transitioned to an inside-forward / striker role over the years, dribbling has naturally become significantly less of a factor in Ronaldo's performances.

Messi also started his footballing career stuck to the by-line, eventually moving to a more central role as his primary position for most of his career. However, Messi plays a very different game to a traditional centre-forward, with his natural Number 10 abilities making him the perfect False 9. As a result Messi comes much deeper, towards the play, rather than making runs and playing off the shoulder of the defenders.

Because he often comes deep to receive the ball, dribbling is still a major part of Messi's game, completing an incredible **4102 dribbles** in the games we have this data for, compared to Ronaldo's **1962 successful dribbles**.

There is therefore little doubt that Lionel Messi is the best when it comes to dribbling.

[More Dribbling Stats](/detailed-stats/successful-dribbles/)

## Who's the best at heading?

Heading is without doubt the most clear-cut category, with Ronaldo's heading stats absolutely dwarfing Messi's.

Over their entire careers, **Ronaldo has scored 158 headers in 1341 appearances**, whereas **Messi has scored just 32 headers in 1181 appearances**.

In addition to headed goals, **Ronaldo has also won 1071 aerial duels** in the games we have this data for, compared to **Messi's 172 aerial duels won**.

Of course, when you look at their respective builds, the way they play, the way their teams play, these numbers are hardly surprising.

[More Aerial Duel Stats](/detailed-stats/aerial-duels/)

## Who's the best at shooting?

The stats show that Ronaldo consistently has more shots on goal than Messi, totalling **5350 shots** in the games we have this data for, compared to Messi's **4346 shots**.

However, **Messi converts a higher percentage of his shots, scoring a goal with every 5.27 shots**, whereas **Ronaldo scores a goal with every 6.43 shots** - this data is for league and Champions League games from 09/10 - 23/24.

Leo Messi also gets more of his shots on target, with **45.88%**, of his efforts on target compared to Ronaldo's **40.28%**,.

However, despite Messi's superior efficiency, the sheer volume of attempts Cristiano Ronaldo is able to produce is incredible and an important skill in itself. He also has the edge in terms of shooting from long-range, as well as with his weak foot and head, so that's enough to call this one a tie.

[More Shooting Stats](/detailed-stats/shot-conversion/)

## Who's the best at penalties?

When it comes to penalties, Ronaldo's numbers are comfortably superior to Messi's, although perhaps not by as much as some people think. The media perception is that Messi is unreliable from the spot, whereas Ronaldo is the ultimate ice-cool penalty king - the truth, is somewhere in between.

Excluding shootouts, **Ronaldo has scored an impressive 184 penalties (with 37 misses)** over his whole career, whereas **Messi has scored 115 penalties (with 35 misses)**.

This gives **Ronaldo an overall penalty conversion rate of 83%**, compared to **Messi's overall penalty conversion rate of 77%**.

Ronaldo's stats are clearly better, however he's not *as* reliable as he is sometimes portrayed, with other elite strikers such as Lewandowski and Ibrahimovic boasting significantly better conversion rates.

In terms of big penalty misses, Messi missed one in the 2016 Copa America final shootout against Chile, and the 2012 Champions League semi-final miss against Chelsea.

For Ronaldo, his biggest penalty misses came in the 2008 Champions League final shootout against Chelsea (his Man Utd side would ultimately go on to win due to John Terry's miss), and in the 2012 Champions League semi-final shootout against Bayern Munich (which did prove fatal for Real Madrid).

[More Penalty Stats](/detailed-stats/penalties/)

## Who's the best at free kicks?

In recent years, Messi has become the ultimate free kick specialist, whilst Ronaldo's proficiency in this area has diminished somewhat alarmingly. However, to say that this category is therefore cut-and-dry is simple recency bias.

For example, it may be true that from **2017-2019**, Messi scored **23** free kick goals to Ronaldo's **5**; however, from **2009-2011**, Ronaldo scored **21** direct free kick goals to Messi's **3**.

In terms of the **all time career** stats, **Messi has now scored 76 free kick goals** compared to **Ronaldo's 65 free kick goals**.

A few years ago this category seemed like a lock for Cristiano Ronaldo, but Leo Messi's stunning turnaround in recent years means he's caught up with Ronaldo and also has the better [free kick conversion](/detailed-stats/free-kicks/) rate.

[More Free Kick Stats](/detailed-stats/free-kicks/)

## Who scores more hat tricks?

The rate at which Messi and Ronaldo score hat tricks is scarcely believable, with a staggering 128between them; **62 career hat tricks for Messi** and **66 career hat tricks for Ronaldo**.

In terms of **frequency**. **Messi scores a hat trick every 19.0 games**, whereas **Ronaldo scores a hat trick every 20.3 games**.

These numbers are so tight, and to add to this, their hat trick count in **league** games is: **39 hat tricks for Messi** and **45 hat-tricks for Ronaldo**. And in the **Champions League**? **8 hat tricks for Messi** and **8 hat tricks for Ronaldo**.

[More Hat-trick Stats](/detailed-stats/hat-tricks/)

## Who has won more individual awards?

No other footballers in history have sustained such elite levels for such a long period of time. Their stranglehold on the coveted **Ballon d'Or** award has been relentless, with **Messi's 8 Ballon d'Or** trophies edging **Ronaldo's haul of 5 Ballons d'Or**. No other player in history has won more than 3! If Messi or Ronaldo didn't have each other to compete with for the award over the years, it's not inconceivable that one of them could have picked up the award 10 times or more.

In terms of UEFA's top award, it's Ronaldo that has the edge with 4 awards (1x UEFA Club Footballer of the Year, 2x UEFA Best Player in Europe, 1x UEFA Men's Player of the Year) to Messi's 3 awards (1x UEFA Club Footballer of the Year, 2x UEFA Best Player in Europe).

In terms of golden boots, Messi has finished as the league's top scorer **8 times**, winning the **European Golden Shoe** on 6 of those occasions. Ronaldo has finished as top scorer in the league **5 times** (once in the Premier League, once in Serie A, and 3 times in La Liga), winning 4 European Golden Shoes in the process.

Ronaldo has won the **Puskas award** for best goal in a calendar year (from 2 nominations), whereas Messi has so far failed to win this award despite being nominated 7 times.

Messi has however won the **Golden Ball**, awarded to the player of the tournament at the World Cup, on two occasions - once in 2014 when he took his side to the final and again in 2022 where he was triumphant. He has also been named Copa America's Best Player on two occasions, and Best Young Player once.

[All Honours & Achievements](/honours-and-achievements/)

## Who has won more trophies?

In terms of **trophies**, Messi has the overall lead, with **49 trophies** to Ronaldo's **37 trophies** (including Messi's 2008 Olympic triumph and 2005 U-20 World Cup).

Internationally, Messi has now won both the Copa America (x2) and the World Cup with Argentina, while Ronaldo has won the Euros with Portugal as well as a Nations League trophy.

Messi has 12 league titles (13 including the MLS Supporters' Shield) to Ronaldo's 7, but Ronaldo has the ascendancy in terms of Champions League triumphs with 5 to Messi's 4. There's not a lot in it, but the overall figures means Messi currently edges this one.

[All Honours & Achievements](/honours-and-achievements/)

## Who has more records?

In short, Messi and Ronaldo have a similar number of records to their name. The most startling is maybe Messi's **Guiness World Record** for scoring **91 goals in a calendar year** in [2012](/calendar-year-stats/2012/). To put this into context, Messi's next best is 60 and Ronaldo's best is 69. To score 91 goals in a year is other worldly.

**Ronaldo however dominates the Champions League record books**, with most goals, most assists, most free kick goals, most hat-tricks (shared with Messi), and most goals in a single season.

**Messi holds many European records at domestic level**, with the most league goals scored in a single season (50 goals), and most consecutive league matches scored in in world football (21 matches, 33 goals).

At International level, **Ronaldo is the all time top scorer with an unbelievable 146 goals**, whilst Messi is the highest scoring South American of all time with **126 goals**.

[All Records](/records/)

## Who's better at international level?

Both players can claim to have enjoyed fantastic careers at international level - their numbers aren't quite as other-wordly as what they produce for their club sides, but they are still extremely impressive nonetheless.

**Ronaldo scores a goal every 128 minutes** for Portugal, and **Messi scores a goal every 137 minutes** for Argentina. When you factor in assists, **Ronaldo makes a goal contribution every 102 minutes**, whereas **Messi makes a goal contribution every 89 minutes**.

Ronaldo is Portugal's all time top scorer with **146 goals** (in 234 appearances), and Messi is Argentina's all-time top scorer with **126 goals** (in 208 appearances).

In terms of individual accolades for the national team, Ronaldo won the **Euro 2021 Golden Boot** for the top scorer, as well as the **Silver Boot at Euro 2016** for scoring the 2nd most goals in the tournament. Messi has won the **World Cup Golden Ball twice (2014 + 2022)** (the only player ever to do so) and the **Copa America Golden Ball twice (2015 & 2021)**, awarded to the best player of those respective tournaments. He also scooped the **Golden Boot award at Copa America 2021** and the **Silver Boot award at the 2022 World Cup**.

Messi has experienced more heartache at international level, losing in 4 major finals, but he was finally able to triumph with his country at full senior level at Copa America 2021. He went on to win the Finalissima trophy (UEFA / CONMEBOL Cup of Champions) in 2022 against European champions Italy, and then won the biggest prize of them all later that year: the World Cup!

In 2024 Messi added a 2nd Copa America trophy, making his Argentina team just the 2nd team in men's internationall football history to win 3 consecutive major tournaments with a World Cup included.

This is in addition to his Olympic Gold medal (with an Argentina U23 side) and the FIFA U20 World Cup trophy.

Ronaldo has reached 2 major international finals with Portugal, winning one of these at the 2016 European Championships, and losing the other at Euro 2004. He also won the UEFA Nations League twice with Portugal (2019 and 2025), and has the most goals in the history of international football!

Ronaldo has the better goalscoring record, but Messi has more individual accolades (4 Best Player awards at major tournaments - the most in history), and has now won both the Copa America and World Cup!
